persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Brian, 19, in Kisumu. Every Saturday you organise football practice for four friends: Otieno, Wanjiku, Baraka and Kevin. Every week you ask in the WhatsApp group who is coming, the answers get lost between other messages, and you never know how many will come. Today you try Who's Coming instead.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called Who's Coming. In about three minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
First, the problem. You want to ask a group one simple question. Sunday lunch at one o'clock, who is coming? Which day for the match? You send it to the group chat.
Then the answers come back mixed with jokes, photos and other messages. Some people answer, some forget. In the end you scroll up and down, counting on your fingers.
Who's Coming solves that. You ask one question to one group, and the app keeps every person's answer on one screen: who said yes, who said no, who said maybe, and who has not answered yet.
Who uses it? A family planning a lunch. A church choir. A football team. Anyone who organises people.
The app was made in America. There is no money in it, and it works the same in Kenya. It uses your phone's normal text messages. Nothing is sent unless you press Send yourself.

lines.t: At the bottom are two tabs. Asks is where your questions are. People is where your groups are.
At the top is the helper line. The first time, it asks for your name and your mobile number. This matters: when a friend answers, the answer comes back to this number.
Start on the People tab. Under New group, type a group name, like Football team, and tap Add group.

lines: The new group appears. Inside it, type a name and tap Add, one person at a time. A mobile number is optional. Or tap Paste a list and type many names, one per line, then tap Add them all.
Under Me, so replies come back to you, you can also type your name and number and tap Save.

lines.t: Now go to the Asks tab and tap the big button, Ask the group something.

lines: Choose who you are asking, then type the question. Then choose how they can answer. Yes, No, Maybe. Or Pick one, where you type the choices, one per line, like Saturday and Sunday. Or In their own words.

Tap Save and send. If your group has mobile numbers, your messages app opens one group text, with a link to tap. You press Send. If nobody has a number, the app copies the message, so you can paste it into WhatsApp.
When a friend taps the link, they see your question with big buttons. Their answer comes back to you as a normal text.

Now the important part. Your question appears as a card on the Asks tab. Next to each person are the answer buttons. When someone tells you their answer, in a text, a call, or face to face, tap their answer on the card. That records it.
The card counts the answers at the top: how many yes, how many no, how many maybe. People with no answer show not yet.
Nudge the quiet ones sends a reminder only to people who have not answered. Copy the tally copies the list of answers. Close puts the question away.
Everything stays on this phone. There is no account, and nobody has to sign up to answer.
To start again, take the tour again under the question mark button and choose Start fresh, then delete anything left. The test tells you exactly how.

In the test, you will be Brian, organising football in Kisumu. You will not need to send any real message. Take your time, and if something is confusing, say so. Confusing parts are exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Brian in Kisumu. The app must start empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press: use what you learned. You do NOT need to send any real message and you do NOT need anyone's real number. If your messages app opens, go back to Who's Coming without pressing Send. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Use the NORMAL app link (not the 🧪 test copy). Open Who’s Coming. This app is not in the house erase list, so there is no 🧹 Start fresh link at the bottom. Instead: 1) If the welcome tour shows by itself, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, tap the ? button at the bottom right → '🎬 Take the tour again' → 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. This removes the example group and question. 2) On the ❓ Asks tab, tap 🗑 on every question that is left → OK. 3) On the 👥 People tab, tap 'Remove group' on every group that is left → OK. (The 'Me' box cannot be emptied; that is fine, the first task changes it.) The Asks tab now says 'Nothing asked yet'. (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this.)

tasks.text: Answers must come back to you. Put in your name, Brian, and your mobile number, 0722 111 222.
tasks.hint: Look on the People tab, in the box called 'Me — so replies come back to you'. Then tap Save.

tasks.text: Make a group called Football team with your four friends in it: Otieno, Wanjiku, Baraka and Kevin. Numbers are not needed.
tasks.hint: On the People tab, make the group first. Then add each friend inside that group's card.

tasks.text: Ask the Football team: Practice on Saturday at 3pm, are you coming? They should be able to answer Yes, No or Maybe.
tasks.hint: On the Asks tab, tap '＋ Ask the group something'. Check 'Who are you asking?' says Football team.

tasks.text: Your friends told you face to face: Otieno is coming, Wanjiku is not coming, and Baraka is not sure. Kevin has not answered. Record this in the app.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('dj_whoscoming_v1')||'null');if(!d||!Array.isArray(d.asks))return false;var gs=d.groups||[];return d.asks.some(function(a){if(a.kind!=='yn')return false;var g=gs.filter(function(x){return x.id===a.groupId})[0];if(!g||!/football/i.test(String(g.name||'')))return false;var A=a.answers||{};function ans(nm){var p=(g.people||[]).filter(function(x){return String(x.name||'').toLowerCase().indexOf(nm)>=0})[0];return p&&A[p.id]?String(A[p.id].a):''}return ans('otieno')==='Yes'&&ans('wanjiku')==='No'&&ans('baraka')==='Maybe'&&ans('kevin')===''})}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Find the practice question's card on the Asks tab. Each friend has their own row of answer buttons.

tasks.text: Also ask the Football team which day is better for the match: Saturday or Sunday. They must choose one of those two days.
tasks.hint: Make a new question, and under 'How can they answer?' choose 'Pick one'. Type each day on its own line.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: ask one group one question, like who is coming
see everyone's answer on one screen: yes, no, maybe, or not yet
it uses your own text messages, and you record or nudge the answers

daily.task: Add one guest in Who’s Coming, or change one guest’s answer.
